articles.title: App+1 | 我做了一个专为「P 人」和 ADHD 设计的精力管理 App
articles.highlight: 在 2018、2019 年左右的少数派，大家曾有一段时间痴迷于折腾各种任务管理软件，我也是其中之一。
articles.summary: 这是少数派 App+1 栏目的一篇文章，作者介绍自己做的精力管理 App，目标用户是 MBTI 中偏「P」的人和 ADHD 人群。作者回顾自己从 2018 年前后开始折腾任务管理工具，先后试过 Things、Sorted 以及各类大而全的知名产品，最终把关注点从「管理任务」转向「管理精力」。对非技术读者来说，它提供了一个观察工具选择思路转变的样本：与其继续换 App，不如先看清自己的注意力与精力节奏。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键启发在于：通用型效率工具默认的使用者状态，未必符合注意力容易波动的人；先明确自己的行为与精力模式，再决定用什么工具，往往比不断更换 App 更有效。

en.highlight: Around 2018 and 2019 on sspai, many of us were briefly obsessed with tinkering with all kinds of task-management software, and I was one of them.
en.summary: In this sspai "App+1" piece, the author introduces an energy-management app he built for people who lean toward the "P" side of MBTI and for users with ADHD. He traces his own path from tinkering with task managers around 2018 — trying Things, Sorted and nearly every well-known, feature-heavy tool — to shifting his focus from managing tasks to managing energy. For a non-technical reader, it is a useful sample of how tool choices can change once you look at your own attention and energy rhythms.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway: general-purpose productivity tools assume a user state that may not fit people whose attention fluctuates; understanding your own behavior and energy patterns first is usually more effective than repeatedly switching apps.
en.title: App+1 | I built an energy-management app for "P-type" people and ADHD

articles.sourceExcerpt: TEACHINGNEURALDECODERS WITHLANGUAGE Xuan Wen1 Yonghao Song1,∗ Yuhong Zhang2 Guoliang Li1 Tzyy-Ping Jung2 Xiaorong Gao1,∗ 1Tsinghua University 2University of California, San Diego ∗Corresponding authors eeyhsong@gmail.com;gxr-dea@tsinghua.edu.cn ABSTRACT Brain–computer interfaces decode neural activity, yet class-label supervision (CLS) leaves relationships among classes implicit. We propose Language as Su- pervision (LaS), which aligns neural features with natural-language class descrip- tions through learned projections and predicts classes using candidate text proto- types. We evaluate seven encoder architectures with independently trained mod- els for visual, motor, and speech decoding from scalp and intracranial recordings.

articles.title: Quoting Geoffrey Huntley
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: No clear evidence
articles.summary: Geoffrey Huntley 指出，当编码智能体没有按约定使用他的诊断库时，光靠内省并更新 AGENTS.md 仍会有偏差，而且会随时间漂移。他的做法是加一个 pre-commit 钩子，扫描 git diff 中绕过诊断模块的可观测性调用，直接让提交失败并把纠正提示注入给智能体，效果立刻变成十分。这个例子说明：与其依赖文档和提示来维持约定，不如把约定变成可自动执行的检查。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键要点是：对智能体的约束最好落在能自动失败、能给出修正信号的机制上，而不是写在会过期的说明文档里。
articles.highlight: 我写一个 pre-commit 钩子，检查 git diff 里是否绕过诊断模块直接调用可观测性模块；一旦发现就让提交失败，并注入提示告诉智能体改用诊断库。
articles.sourceExcerpt: If the agent isn't using my diagnostics library, I could introspect and update AGENTS.md, but there's still a delta, and it'll drift. Instead, I write a pre-commit hook that checks the git diff for direct calls to observability modules that bypass my diagnostics module. Boom: fail the commit, inject a prompt telling the agent to use the diagnostics library.

en.highlight: I write a pre-commit hook that checks the git diff for direct calls to observability modules that bypass my diagnostics module. Boom: fail the commit, inject a prompt telling the agent to use the diagnostics library.
en.summary: Geoffrey Huntley notes that when a coding agent fails to use his diagnostics library, introspecting and updating AGENTS.md still leaves a delta, and it will drift over time. His answer is a pre-commit hook that scans the git diff for observability calls bypassing his diagnostics module, fails the commit, and injects a corrective prompt to the agent — which immediately made it ten out of ten. The lesson: keep agent conventions in automatically enforced checks rather than in documentation and prompts that decay.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway: constrain agents with mechanisms that can fail automatically and feed back a correction, not with instructions that go stale.
en.title: Don't Just Update AGENTS.md: Use a Pre-Commit Hook to Force Agents to Use Your Diagnostics Library
